title: Phantom capacity from delayed decommission signals triggered fallback amplification
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: A backlog in the decommission signal pipeline produced stale 'available capacity' state for a decommissioning region. Traffic continued to be routed there for a short window, creating hot shards. Hot shard rebalancing then pushed load into fallback variants/tiers and cross-region routes, amplifying latency and causing an elevated rate of model-variant fallbacks across multiple customers. This ticket documents the incident, mitigations, and follow-ups.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-05 at ~09:42 UTC our autoscaling/decommission controller experienced a flurry of delayed tombstone events after a transient Kafka partitioning incident. The control-plane cache reconciler used stale node availability and reported >0 capacity for region eu-west-2 for ~18 minutes despite nodes being in the process of decommissioning. The routing layer continued to schedule requests into the region, which caused localized queueing and KV cache pressure. The runtime began triggering fallback policies to model variants and lower-tier pools; fallbacks cascaded into other regions that then exceeded their local SLOs. The outcome: ~13% increase in 95th percentile latency and 7 customer-impacting errors on production API keys during the window.
timeline: 2026-03-05T09:40Z - Grafana alerts: regional latency surge for eu-west-2 routes
2026-03-05T09:42Z - Pager duty triggered; ops began initial investigation
2026-03-05T09:48Z - Observed control-plane write errors in Kafka consumer group; decommission tombstones lagging
2026-03-05T09:55Z - Temporary routing rule applied to stop routing new requests to eu-west-2 (manual override)
2026-03-05T10:04Z - Autoscaler removed inflight traffic via graceful drain; KV cache pressure subsided
2026-03-05T10:20Z - Normalization: fallback rates returned to baseline; alert resolved at 10:30Z
2026-03-06 - Post-incident deep-dive kickoff; data capture and replay prepared
root_cause: A transient Kafka partition rebalance caused the decommission signal consumer to lag. The control-plane reconciler did not treat a consumer lag beyond the configured threshold as authoritative 'no-capacity' and instead continued to serve stale node state into the routing topology. This subtle race between decommission tombstones and the reconciler cache allowed phantom capacity to persist for ~18 minutes.
immediate_mitigation: Applied manual routing override to stop new traffic to eu-west-2
Restarted the decommission consumer and forced an immediate cache invalidation in the control plane
Scoped temporary reduction of circuit-breaker thresholds to prevent downstream variant amplification
long_term_fixes: Control-plane: add consumer-lag health gating — if consumer lag > configured threshold mark region as 'draining' and stop routing
Reconciler: add tombstone validation window and cross-check with node heartbeats before reporting available capacity
Routing: implement conservative routing decay after decommission events (soft-stop then hard-stop after 30s) to avoid routing into partially-decommissioned pools
Observability: add a dedicated Grafana panel for decommission signal lag and anomaly alert with runbook linking to auto-override action
Chaos testing: add fault-injection test that simulates message-broker partitions and verifies routing behavior under decommission delays

ENG-93121 - Reconciler cross-check with heartbeat service (owner: M. Alvarez)
ENG-93122 - Conservatively throttle routing towards recently signaled decommissioning regions (owner: infra team)
PM-441 - Update incident runbook and customer comms templates (owner: L. Nguyen)
DES-204 - Console panel redesign to surface decommission health metrics (owner: R. Patel)
Create postmortem writeup and share in #incidents with timeline and graph snapshots
lessons_learned: Small control-plane telemetry gaps can have outsized client impact because routing decisions are binary and amplify when fallbacks trigger. Improving safety guards around decommission events (circuit-breakers and gating on consumer lag) and surfacing these signals to SRE/eng teams reduces blast radius. We also learned that automatic fallbacks should prefer local rate-limited drains before cross-region failovers.
qa_and_validation: Added unit tests for consumer-lag detection, integration tests that replay tombstone lag scenarios, and a staging canary with the gating feature enabled. QA run: synthetic traffic injected against a staging cluster while simulating Kafka partition event; outcome verified no routing into draining region and no cascade fallbacks.
communication_and_customers: On 2026-03-05 the incidents team sent incident summaries to affected customers via the status page and initiated support outreach for customers with SLAs. A follow-up customer-facing incident report will be posted after engineering changes land in runtime-1.24.
closure_notes: All immediate mitigations completed during the incident window. Long-term fixes are tracked as follow-up ENG tickets. The gating change and reconciler cross-checks are targeted for runtime-1.24 (shiproom: 2026-04). Postmortem reviewed and accepted by Reliability org on 2026-03-12.
